import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np

# Load the data
customer_segments = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Select relevant columns
segments = ['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']
customer_segments = customer_segments[['ID', 'Z_Revenue'] + segments]

# Melt the DataFrame for easier plotting
customer_segments = pd.melt(customer_segments, id_vars='ID', value_vars=segments, value_name='Product_Spending')

# Group by product and calculate the mean revenue
revenue_by_product = customer_segments.groupby('variable')['value'].mean().reset_index()

# Plot a bar chart
plt.figure(figsize=(10, 6))
sns.barplot(x='variable', y='value', data=customer_segments, hue='variable', dodge=False)

# Add title and labels
plt.title('Product Spending by Revenue')
plt.xlabel('Product')
plt.ylabel('Average Revenue')
plt.xticks(rotation=90)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
